DEFINITION · qeva:1:symmetry@2

Symmetry

A transformation that leaves a specified object unchanged relative to a specified action.

editorialsymmetry · structure
Run a related experimentTrace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

Symmetry is never just “looks the same”: one must specify which transformations are allowed and what counts as unchanged.

EXACT

The compact statement

The symmetry group of x relative to the action of G on X is Stab_G(x) = { g in G : g·x = x }.

Example

A square in the Euclidean plane has rotations and reflections that map the square to itself.

Boundary / caveat

Symmetry depends on the chosen object representation and transformation group.

Assumptions

  • A group G acts on a set X.
  • An object x belongs to X.
